03Problem Statement03 / 16
Self-directed learners commit to a fixed plan — “two hours a day, finish by the 30th” — then reality drifts within days, and the plan never adjusts.
01Who & where it hurts. Online-course, exam-prep and self-study learners, with no instructor to set the pace. Time-trackers only record; static planners never revise — neither learns the pace you actually achieve.
02Why it bites. The finish date silently goes stale, yet the plan keeps showing it as if valid. The learner gets no trustworthy signal of how far off-track they are.
03What makes it hard. Evidence is sparse — a handful of sessions before the first replan — and pace is non-stationary. The method must work from little data and tell a real shift from noise.
04The gap we close. A planner that treats your own logged behaviour as evidence, updates its pace estimate as evidence arrives, and regenerates the plan.
04Abstract & Scope04 / 16
An adaptive study-planning system for a single self-directed learner — plus an honest evaluation of the algorithms behind it.
01In scope · Phase-1. The open-loop adaptive planner — pace calibration, change detection, completion projection, and capacity-based replanning — realised in a working, local-first web app.
02Rigorously evaluated. Every component compared offline against established baselines on synthetic data with known ground truth: held-out archetypes · bootstrap CIs · Holm/Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
03Out of scope · for now. Closing the loop with verified learning, longitudinal real-data validation, and multi-user / institutional settings — these are Phase-2 and beyond.
05Literature Survey05 / 16
APPROACH FAMILY · CLICK
STRENGTH
THE GAP FOR THIS PROJECT
Bayesian calibration
Works from sparse per-learner data; interpretable and fair across groups
Targets correctness — not planned-vs-actual pace
Change-point detection
Detects behavioural shifts early; grounded in statistical process control
Detects only — prescribes no replanning
Gaussian-process projection
Calibrated uncertainty; degrades gracefully with little data
Applied cross-sectionally, not to a longitudinal burn-up
Adaptive scheduling base paper
Fast, prerequisite-aware; adaptation shown to help
Plan solved once — no feedback from realised pace
SRL analytics
Validated trace-based indicators of self-regulation
Measures behaviour — not tied to replanning
Each technique is strong in isolation — none closes the loop from realised pace back to the plan. That loop is the contribution.
Islam 2024 (base paper) · Chen 2024 · Saqr 2026 · Pérez-Suay 2024 · Alhazbi 2024 — and 16 more surveyed in the report.
06Suggestions from Review-306 / 16
FROM MY GUIDE · REVIEW-3
Explore LLM-guided practice sessions
A live LLM watches the learner’s work in a practice / test session — e.g. the code they’re writing — and guides: nudges when they’re stuck, suggests improvements. Copilot-like in mechanism, but it never completes the work for them.
→ scoped as a Phase-2 exploration (slide 15)
SELF-INITIATED SINCE REVIEW-3 · CLICK
Redesigned the scheduler
Retired the brittle day-by-day packer for a capacity-based booking model, and re-validated calibration, detection & projection on the new regime. (Ch 4.4)
Made the evaluation defensible
Held-out learner archetypes, bootstrap CIs, Holm/BH correction — and reported the nulls honestly. (Ch 4.3, 6)
Grounded the synthetic data
The generator is calibrated against the OULAD public dataset so the regime resembles real behaviour. (Ch 5.2)

Every model was chosen by offline comparison, not by assumption.
✓ REAL WIN
The context-shrinkage calibrator beats the Bayesian incumbent on prospective, short-history pace — the low-data regime the planner depends on. Holm-surviving.
○ HONEST NULL
No exotic detector beats the CUSUM frontier. So we ship CUSUM — the fastest — because detection only raises a human-confirmed prompt.
⚑ VALIDATED, NOT YET SHIPPED · CLICK
Split-conformal restores the GP interval’s coverage (raw GP under-covers badly). Validated now, shipped in Phase-2.
Per-component metrics · bootstrap CIs · Holm/Benjamini–Hochberg · oracle as an upper-bound ceiling. A dynamic-programming scheduler won on deadline drift, but was retired with the day-by-day design — evaluated, deliberately not shipped.
08Design Approach & Constraints08 / 16
KEY DECISIONS
01Local-first & event-sourced. Every action is an immutable event in the browser (IndexedDB); every view is derived by replaying the log. The core loop works offline, and each learner gets an isolated per-user database.
02Split compute by need. Model-fitting over accumulated history runs in a Python service (Bayesian + shrinkage calibration, CUSUM); views derived from the local log run in the browser (GP projection, booking, dashboards).
03One behaviour, two implementations. The TypeScript client engine is mirrored by a Python engine, kept numerically aligned by a golden-fixture parity harness — so the evaluated code is the shipped code.
Constraints & assumptions — single learner · commodity CPU-only hardware · sparse data (few sessions before the first replan). Every service call carries a signed token, verified before any model runs; results return in seconds, with a stale-cache fallback. Dependencies — Supabase (auth · database · storage) is the data hub; an offline research pipeline supplies the selected models and parameters, and is not in the request path.
09System Architecture09 / 16
Three tiers — local-first React client (terracotta) · Python intelligence service (moss) · Supabase data hub (clay) · offline research tier (dashed, not in the request path). Diagram grounded in the actual codebase. Click to enlarge.

15What’s Next · Phase-215 / 16
01
Verified learning — the principal novelty
Generate concept-tagged assessments from the learner’s own material with an LLM, estimate genuine mastery with cold-start knowledge tracing, and feed verified mastery back into pace calibration — replacing gameable self-reported time. This closes the loop.
02
LLM-guided practice sessions — guide-suggested
Live, Socratic in-session coaching that watches the learner’s work and nudges — never completes. #1 verifies learning after a session; #2 supports it during one.
03
Ship the validated refinement
The split-conformal correction that fixes the GP interval’s under-coverage — validated in Phase-1.
04
Longitudinal validation
Adaptive vs static on a real learner’s own logged sessions: schedule adherence and measured learning gain.
TIMELINE Aug 1 · Phase-2 start→ Aug–Sep · build→ Sep 20–Oct 25 · Phase-2 ESA
Scope is prioritized — the verified-learning loop is the core deliverable; guided practice is exploratory.
